topic: Pick the AI model by task, quality, speed and cost

cover.concept: Studio still life on flat teal: four tools in a row, a scalpel, a sledgehammer, a stopwatch and a small stack of coins.
cover.lineDraft: Not every task needs the biggest model.

slides.label: The mistake
slides.idea: Using one model for everything wastes time and credits

slides.label: Ask 1
slides.idea: Task first: a quick edit and a hard bug need different models

slides.label: Ask 2
slides.idea: Quality: how bad is it if the answer is wrong?

slides.label: Ask 3
slides.idea: Speed: fast models for small loops you repeat

slides.label: Ask 4
slides.idea: Cost: credits and limits run out; spend them on hard problems

slides.label: Cheat sheet
slides.idea: Quick edit → fast model; hard bug → strongest; big repo → long context; practice → cheapest
friend who says "I just use whatever's free"

images.name: cover
images.prompt: Photoreal studio still life, magazine-ad quality, crisp soft light, subtle film grain. On a flat, seamless, saturated teal backdrop: four tools lie in a neat row, a small steel scalpel, a heavy sledgehammer, a silver stopwatch and a short stack of copper coins. The tools sit in the lower 60% of the frame; the top 35% is plain teal backdrop. Portrait 2:3, natural colours. No readable text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no faces, no watermark.
